items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The fix is two lines inside single_alias. The condition `all(self.query.alias_refcount[a] == 0 ...)` reads plainly. It has no comment explaining why, but the rubric still counts a minor documentation gap like this as perfect.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: It reuses the existing query.get_initial_alias() inside single_alias and leaves Collector and QuerySet.delete alone. The guard isn't strictly needed. The added test leaves a trailing blank line at the end of tests/delete/tests.py. Both are cosmetic.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No exception handling is involved and no magic constants are added. Only the alias-count logic changes, and all hidden tests passed (F2P 1/1, P2P 52/52).

items.name: Subquery dropped only for genuine single-table deletes
items.name_zh: 仅在真正单表删除时去掉子查询
items.evidence: The root cause is fixed in single_alias by registering the base alias before counting. The agent checked that `filter(avatar__desc='a')` still produces the pk IN subquery with joins. There is no backend-specific branch, so the MySQL compiler that uses single_alias benefits too.
